Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase! The players make their way out to the middle.
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Netherlands were excellent with the ball for most parts! Daniel Doram and the pacers bowled really well for the first 15 overs. It was the back end though where their bowlers went the distance or they would have been well in control of this game. Still though, they have a strong batting line-up and will back themselves to chase this down. Ireland on the other hand, will know the wicket is not the easiest and if they bowl the right lines and lengths, this can be defended. Chase in a bit.

That is a fine recovery from Ireland! Had they been given 150 after the 14th over, pretty sure they would have taken it. However, their batting just never got going. They lost three quick wickets but Lorcan Tucker along with the middle order got them to safer shores. However, they yet again lost three in quick succession and were big trouble when George Dockrell! Mark Adair and Gareth Delany though batted brilliantly. Mark Adair was the aggressor and Gareth Delany gave him able support. They have taken them to a score which we feel is par.

OUT! TAKEN! A wicket on the last ball and Tim Pringle has comeback very strongly. Shorter and on middle, Gareth Delany looks to hit it down the ground but mistimes it and it is taken at long off. Ireland END WITH 150!

TOSS - NETHERLANDS HAVE WON THE TOSS AND ELECTED TO FIELD!

Ireland will head into this one as favourites. They too will be confident after their show against Pakistan. They did lose the series but they really played a good brand of cricket. They too have a lot of quality in their ranks and they'll be eager to do well in this tournament. We have seen these sides play out thrillers and we expect another one. Stay tuned for the toss in a bit.

It is time for the second game of the tri-series and this time it is the Irish who'll be going up against the home side, Netherlands. ... MATCH DAY ...

Match number 2 of the 2024 Netherlands T20I Tri-Series is upon us, featuring a face-off between the Netherlands and Ireland at the Voorburg Cricket Club in The Hague. The Netherlands have kicked off their campaign with a win over Scotland, and the Irish will be aiming to do the same. In their last T20I assignment, Ireland faced a narrow 2-1 series defeat against Pakistan, but not without putting up a commendable fight. After drawing first blood in the series, Paul Stirling and his men struggled to capitalise on key moments, leading to losses in the subsequent games. Andy Balbirnie and Lorcan Tucker showed glimpses of promise in different matches, although Ireland's batting overall left much to be desired. Skipper Paul Stirling failed to make a significant impact and will be eager to rectify this in the current series, as will Harry Tector. Curtis Campher, too, had a challenging time with both bat and ball and will be looking to make a notable contribution in this series. On the bowling front, Mark Adair was a standout performer, and the team will hope for more consistent support from the likes of Craig Young and Ben White. As for the Netherlands, it was a well-rounded effort that saw them secure a comfortable win in the series opener. Michael Levitt and Vikramjit Singh stood out with the bat and will look to carry their form into the game against Ireland. Max O'Dowd and Scott Edwards struggled to come to terms with the surface during their innings and will look to make amends. With the ball, whether it was the pace unit or the spin bowling unit, the Dutch were clinical in both departments. Vivian Kingma and Logan van Beek got the ball to zip through and broke the back of the Scottish batting unit, while the spin duo of Aryan Dutt and Daniel Doram played their part effectively. Scott Edwards will be hoping for a similar effort from his team as they aim to make it two wins out of two. Given the strength of Ireland on paper, the Netherlands are expected to face a sterner test. Will the Dutch rise to the challenge? We shall find out.
